resources.string: This app doesn\'t contain Noita: it runs your own copy of the game, the Windows version of Jan 25 2025 from GOG (build %1$s) or Steam, recompiled for Android. On the right is what it still needs. Once everything is there, the app goes straight into the game.
Not ready yet: see the items marked ✕.
Granted. The game is read from %1$s, and saves are kept there too.
Needed to read the game from shared storage, where you can copy it over USB, and to keep saves when the app is reinstalled. Android calls it \"All files access\".
Checked once storage access is granted.

Copy everything in your Noita folder (the one with noita.exe in it) into %1$s. Over USB, that\'s Internal storage › noitadroid › Noita; the folder is already there. With adb, tools/android/push_game.sh does it.
%1$s has part of the game, but not: %2$s. Copy the whole Noita folder (the one with noita.exe in it).
data/data.wak is %1$s, but should be %2$s: the copy isn\'t complete (or is still going).
Checked once the game files are there.
%1$s isn\'t from a build this app takes: Noita for Windows of Jan 25 2025, from GOG (build %2$s) or Steam. Other builds don\'t work.
This app was built without FMOD, so the game is silent. FMOD\'s license doesn\'t allow sharing it: whoever builds the app adds it (tools/android/setup_fmod.sh). Not needed to play.
To a zip, or from one (Windows saves too).
The game is silent: FMOD isn\'t imported yet. Setting it up restarts the game, so first use Save & Quit in the game\'s own menu.
Off: touching the screen acts as a mouse.
Auto: shown, as no gamepad is connected.
Auto: hidden, as a gamepad is connected.

Drag the controls about over the paused game. They show while you play; the menus have none in their way, and the inventory only the button that closes it. Touching anywhere else stays a mouse: for menus, the inventory and pointing at things.
Drag a control. Tap one to size or hide it.
Pick a button, then the one it should act as: the two swap. For the game only; the sticks, D-pad and triggers stay. The game\'s own settings can rebind its actions too.
The button it takes over gets its old role.
This device has %1$d prime, %2$d big and %3$d small cores.
This device has %1$d big and %2$d small cores, and no single fastest one: there\'s nothing to choose.
This device\'s %1$d cores are all alike: there\'s nothing to choose.
Android puts the game\'s threads on any core.
Prime core for the main thread
The game\'s main thread has the fastest core to itself, its simulation threads the others. 8–16% faster in our tests.
As above, and one more simulation thread uses the fastest core while the main thread waits. Another 8–13% faster in our tests, and a little hotter.
Applies at once. The number of simulation threads follows the next time the game starts.
Exported (%1$s), as the game last saved: it saves the run when you save and quit.
It replaces the current save, which is kept as save00.backup-(date) in the saves folder. The game restarts with the imported save.
Not there yet, but GOG\'s installer is: %1$s in %2$s. The app can unpack it into %3$s and build the game from it.

Put GOG\'s offline installer (setup_noita_20250125-1640_….exe) in Download, or copy everything in your Noita folder (the one with noita.exe in it) into %1$s. If it\'s somewhere else, a memory card say, choose the installer or noita.exe.
Built on this device, from your copy of the game.
Built on this device once the game files are there.
The game\'s code is made from your own copy of the game, here on this device. It takes about 16 minutes, once.
This version of the app needs the game\'s code built again (about 16 minutes).
It was built from a different copy of the game: build it again from this one.

The app turns your noita.exe into code for this device. It takes about 16 minutes, and the processor runs at full speed: the device gets hot, so take it out of its case. You can use other apps meanwhile, but don\'t close Noita from the recent apps. If the build stops, the next one goes on where it left off.

The app unpacks GOG\'s installer into Internal storage › noitadroid › Noita (about 3 minutes, 1.7 GB), then turns your noita.exe into code for this device (about 16 minutes). The processor runs at full speed: the device gets hot, so take it out of its case. You can use other apps meanwhile, but don\'t close Noita from the recent apps. If it stops, it goes on where it left off.
The charger isn\'t connected, and building uses a lot of battery: better plug it in.
Stopped. What was finished is kept: the next build goes on from there.
The build failed: %1$s. Its log is in Internal storage › noitadroid › build.log.
the built code doesn\'t check out
not enough space in %1$s: %2$d MB needed, %3$d MB free
This device has no file picker.
%1$s isn\'t something the app can use: choose GOG\'s installer (setup_noita_….exe), noita.exe in a game folder, or FMOD\'s Android download.
The app can\'t open %1$s from there. Choose it in the storage\'s own folders (Internal storage, or the memory card).
Not in %1$s yet. Found on this device:
GOG\'s installer is here too: %1$s in %2$s. The app can install the game from it instead.
GOG\'s installer is still in %1$s (%2$s); the game doesn\'t need it any more.
%1$s (%2$s) in %3$s. Keep it if you\'d rather not download it again to install another time.
FMOD %1$s, imported from your own download.
Without FMOD the game is silent. Its license doesn\'t allow the app to include it, but you can import your own download: %1$s, in %2$s.
Without FMOD the game is silent; it\'s optional. Download FMOD 2.01.23 for Android here (74 MB), or choose your own fmodstudioapi201…android.tar.gz.
Importing FMOD from %1$s… the app then restarts.
this is FMOD %1$s; the game needs 2.01.x
